cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T5 takes up T4's 'social weight'; T6 answers T5's 'demand'.
cells.limitation: Replies are one-line rebuttals; T2 ignores T1's testing argument entirely.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T6 distinguishes responsiveness from demanded effort; T7 builds the nudge on it.
cells.limitation: T4 restates T1; new distinctions stay single sentences, never worked through.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: Ledger versus authenticity tension runs T1 through T8.
cells.limitation: Nobody weighs risking a 'lovely' friendship by raising it, or the friend's possible reasons.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T9 folds T8's 'their nature is different' into understanding over changing.
cells.limitation: T7 'Exactly' merges two minds without qualification; T8's mind never moves.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: Section E sharpens to passive-but-caring versus indifferent friend.
cells.limitation: Section D claims a clarified motive the debate never examined.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T6 accurately reframes T5's 'demand' as a need for responsiveness.
cells.limitation: T2 and T5 reduce T1's reciprocity view to a ledger and transaction.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T8 objects that nudging trains performance rather than revealing care.
cells.limitation: T4's 'survive real stress' and T5's 'lost the freedom' are asserted, not reasoned.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T2's dancing-star line roughly matches Zarathustra's Prologue.
cells.limitation: T1 says user never tested reciprocity, contradicting the stated silence; T6 overstates neglect.

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: Section E frames outcomes conditionally on the friend's nature.
cells.limitation: T7 'they will respond' and Section D motive stated as fact.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T9 drops changing behaviour in favour of understanding the friend.
cells.limitation: No mind concedes a point; T8's challenge to nudging goes unanswered by T7's mind.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern
cells.example: T3 reads the concern as whether the user is valued.
cells.limitation: Never asks whether the user wants more initiative, reassurance or proof of care.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: T9's 'miss hearing from them' fits the texting detail.
cells.limitation: T1 ignores that the user already stopped texting; 'lovely' meetings never used.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: T9 centres understanding the friend over winning effort.
cells.limitation: Speakers' values replace the user's; the user's own priorities never sought.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: T4 names the risk of a lopsided dynamic solidifying.
cells.limitation: Cost of awkwardness or losing a lovely friendship unweighed; Section A invents 'struggling'.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: Section E branches on passive versus indifferent friend, each with implication.
cells.limitation: Friendship length, friend's circumstances, initiative with others never asked or branched.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: T3 suggests the user wants to be valued for presence.
cells.limitation: T3 and Section D assert the user's motive as fact; no alternatives offered.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T8 surfaces that initiating may reflect nature, not care.
cells.limitation: The user's reading of silence as indifference is never put to them directly.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: Section D names exchange-balance versus accepting temperament.
cells.limitation: Values belong to the minds; no question asks which matters more to the user.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T3 hints at a need to feel valued.
cells.limitation: Fear of rejection or seeming needy never named; T6 'neglect' edges toward alarm.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: Section E lets the user test which branch is true.
cells.limitation: Few distinctions offered as questions; the debate tells rather than invites.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options
cells.example: Nudge (T7), direct truth (T8), express missing them (T9).
cells.limitation: Accepting the pattern, waiting, or stepping back never laid out as options.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs
cells.example: T8 notes nudging may only train performance.
cells.limitation: No cost of speaking up or of staying silent is spelled out.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: Section E: observe whether behaviour shifts after the conversation.
cells.limitation: Does not say what shift would count or what each would favour next.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: Section E isolates the friend's nature as the key unknown.
cells.limitation: 'Will likely resolve' overstates; friend's circumstances left unconsidered.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps
cells.example: T9 and Section E: say you miss hearing from them, then observe.
cells.limitation: No guidance on framing so the friend does not feel accused.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T9 is plain and direct.
cells.limitation: 'Social weight' (T4) and 'secure base' (T3) left abstract.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T5 names T4's 'social weight' explicitly.
cells.limitation: T7 'Exactly' leaves unclear which part of T6 is endorsed.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Nine short turns, all within range.
cells.limitation: Uniformly brief turns leave no room to develop any point.

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices
cells.example: Reciprocity, authenticity, security positions stay distinct.
cells.limitation: One formal register and near-equal lengths across all minds, T1 to T9.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: No recaps; debate is compact.
cells.limitation: T4 largely repeats T1's untested-reciprocity point.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension
cells.example: T4 warns the bond may not survive real stress.
cells.limitation: Stakes of losing a lovely friendship never dramatised or felt.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals
cells.example: T9 shifts from changing behaviour to understanding the friend.
cells.limitation: No reversal occurs; no mind changes position.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice
cells.example: T2's 'Stop calculating' gives Nietzsche's mind some edge.
cells.limitation: Reciprocity and Attachment minds sound alike and flat.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T8 'merely training them to perform' is sharp.
cells.limitation: No analogy or concrete example from friendship life.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement
cells.example: T8 to T9 softens the tone toward the friend.
cells.limitation: Flat, even rhythm throughout; no build or release.

strengths: Section E gives a usable conditional: passive-but-caring versus indifferent friend, with an observable test.
T6 introduces responsiveness versus demanded effort, and T7 builds on it.
T9 offers a proportionate, gentle next step: say you miss hearing from them.
weaknesses: T1 and T4 ignore that the user already stopped texting and saw nothing happen.
Section D and T3 assert the user's motive as fact; no alternatives offered.
No costs of speaking up or staying silent; no mind concedes or changes position.

symptoms.observed: Claims the user has not tested reciprocity, though the user already stopped texting.
symptoms.evidence: you are failing to test if your friend feels the same

symptoms.observed: Section D and T3 assert one motive as fact, offer no alternatives.
symptoms.evidence: You are checking if the relationship is a secure base

symptoms.observed: Options proposed without costs of speaking up or of staying quiet.
symptoms.evidence: A polite nudge is not a demand

symptoms.observed: Predicts the friend's response with certainty.
symptoms.evidence: they will respond to the nudge by initiating next time

symptoms.observed: Authenticity mind never moves; no mind revises after an objection.
symptoms.evidence: you are merely training them to perform

findings.description: States the user never tests reciprocity; the user reported stopping texting and nothing happening.
Declares the user's frustration stems from a need for mutual affirmation; the user never stated this.
Certain prediction that a caring friend will initiate after a nudge.
Cialdini's reciprocity is a compliance principle; applying it as friendship obligation is a stretch.
Dancing-star line is a loose paraphrase of Zarathustra's Prologue, used out of context.

rubric_fit_notes: The minimal-length debate (9 short turns) limits several cells at once; scored per distinct effect. Nietzsche paraphrase judged close enough not to warrant a cap.
question_type_note: Read as a decision about whether to raise the imbalance, so options, costs and conditions were weighed as written.
